content.objective: Generate a complete, industry-standard, secure, scalable, bug-free authentication system using Next.js (App Router), TailwindCSS, secure cookies, and JWT-based authentication.

technology_stack.frontend_backend: Next.js App Router (Frontend + Backend in same project)
technology_stack.styling: TailwindCSS with global color + size configuration
technology_stack.authentication: Access Token + Refresh Token token-based authentication
technology_stack.security: HTTP-only cookies for refresh token, context for access token, role-based routing

requirements.1: Create a fully robust, fast, reliable, scalable, and performance-optimized authentication system.
requirements.2: Generate all required Next.js app folders, API routes, middleware, util functions, and components.
requirements.3: Strictly NO BUGS, no conflicts, no errors — production-ready code only.
requirements.4: Include three layouts: PublicLayout (no login), UserLayout (for users), AdminLayout (for admins).
requirements.5: Admin role can access both UserLayout and AdminLayout. User role can only access UserLayout.
requirements.6: Create login page and register page with Tailwind CSS modern UI.
requirements.7: Use context to store accessToken — DO NOT store accessToken in localStorage.
requirements.8: Store refreshToken in secure HTTP-only cookie with SameSite rules depending on environment.
requirements.11: When accessToken expires, automatically call refreshToken API to get new accessToken.
requirements.12: If refreshToken is expired → logout user + delete refreshToken cookie.
requirements.13: On browser refresh → context resets → call refreshToken API automatically to restore user session.
requirements.14: Logout removes both accessToken and refreshToken (cookie).
requirements.15: Ensure refreshToken is NEVER visible in network tab, devtools, or frontend.
requirements.16: All sensitive data must be hidden using industry security practices.
requirements.17: Do not expose refreshToken or secrets anywhere.
requirements.18: All logic must be secure for both development and production.

output_expectations.1: Provide complete folder structures in tree format.
output_expectations.12: ▪ Auth API routes (login, register, refresh, logout)
output_expectations.16: ▪ Database user model (Prisma or Mongo — choose best automatically unless user specifies)

architecture_principles.1: Zero bugs — all code must be clean, optimized, and consistent.
architecture_principles.3: Error handling must be central and reusable.
architecture_principles.4: Write comments explaining every important function.
architecture_principles.5: Show both development and production cookie settings.
architecture_principles.6: Code must be scalable for large systems.

response_format.summary: Overview of what has been generated.
response_format.steps: All steps needed to integrate the auth system.
response_format.testing_notes: How to test in development and production.
response_format.deployment_notes: How to deploy on Vercel with secure cookies.

special_instructions.1: If anything missing for a perfect authentication system → automatically add it.
special_instructions.2: Always optimize for security, performance, and scalability.
special_instructions.3: If there is a better approach (industry-standard), automatically apply it.
special_instructions.4: Ensure production cookie rules for Vercel + HTTPS.
special_instructions.5: Ensure refreshToken never appears in devtools or network inspector.
special_instructions.6: Ensure user session persists across refresh for 30 days.

content.example_query: Build the complete authentication system described above for my Next.js project.

example_response.summary: A complete industry-level authentication system with layouts, token rotation, context handling, secure cookies, and role-based routing.
example_response.notes: Follows OWASP authentication, session, and cookie security standards.
